targetEvidence.text: # Agent Coordination

The former coordination engine was retired in `2180b4e72701bb090288af8fe8021008d9d42079`. `coordination` is not a current public CLI verb; the actual machine-readable `--help --json` manifest is the CLI inventory.

CollaborationPattern owns Unit collaboration patterns in `src/runner/execution/patterns/index.mjs`; Unit execution enters through `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`. Workflow execution belongs to `src/workflow/runner.mjs` and its Unit execution-core integration.

The surviving Assignment/Run dispatch chain is also current: Assignment building, DispatchPlan compilation, governed execution and RunResult normalization are owned by `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs`, `plan.mjs`, `assignment-runner.mjs` and `run-result.mjs`.

The [complete previous portal](history/retired-engine/README.md#literal-snapshot) and [previous spec](history/retired-engine/spec.md#literal-snapshot) remain verbatim, including all original qualifications and statuses. They are non-authority history, not present implementation claims.
Use the snapshots to audit preserved claims. They do not reinstate the retired engine or strengthen proposal/implementation status.
- [Historical architecture](history/retired-engine/architecture/system-context.md#literal-snapshot)
The retired engine no longer defines this area's live runtime. Current material
is narrower, but not empty: it retains the dispatch/result/recovery boundaries
that have surviving executable owners, and four cognitive companions consumed

targetEvidence.text: # Host Invocation

Host invocation defines how a selected fgOS runtime accepts a request from a host surface, normalizes it into a semantic operation when the route is native, selects a provider, grants capability, invokes the provider, records lifecycle evidence, and projects the result back to the caller.
Use this area when work touches:
- CLI, remote, or chat host entry behavior after a runtime is selected;
| Reader goal | Read |
| Understand the full direction | [vision.md](vision.md) |
| Layer | Status | Meaning |

| Existing Node CLI payload | `legacy-current` | `bin/fgos.mjs` and the current Node package still carry existing CLI behavior. The file remains unmoved and is the legacy payload during Rust host migration. |
Host invocation owns this question:
How does an already selected fgOS runtime admit, route, invoke, and present
semantic operations across host surfaces and provider mechanisms?
No component-boundary change.

This documentation migration promotes an existing host/surface concern into the platform docs structure. It does not create, rename, split, merge, or reassign a platform component. The existing whole-system boundary entry is [Host And Surface Layer](../component-boundary.md#4-current-high-level-components).
| Status | Meaning |
| `current` | Implemented current behavior that is part of the target shape. |
Every design claim in this area must have an implementation status or a proof gap. The tracking table lives in [verification/implementation-alignment.md](verification/implementation-alignment.md).

The old documents under [../../architect/host-invocation-routing/](../../architect/host-invocation-routing/) remain legacy/current sources until redirected or drained. Do not delete them in this migration pass.

The preservation ledger must be checked after each phase. A detail omitted from prose is only safe when [intent-preservation-ledger.md](intent-preservation-ledger.md) records whether it was promoted, split, kept legacy, redirected, archived, deferred, superseded, rejected, or remains unknown.
| Relationship | File |
| full direction | [vision.md](vision.md) |

Added in candidate: the [retired documentation migration policy](history/documentation-migration/documentation-standardization-plan.md) is retained verbatim as non-authority history, not as the area's current documentation policy. The source inventory names that carrier.

The candidate restoration notes distinguish literal selected-design text from checked implementation. In particular, contract range intersection and transport alternatives are not certified as implemented; performance budgets are not measurements; the old npm-bin removal clause is flagged rather than replacing the retained compatibility ownership rule. Existing September preview records are dated evidence, not a fresh current-route or release certification. Independent checkpoint conservation and the current-unit truth sample are still pending.

targetEvidence.text: # Packaging-Distribution
Packaging-distribution explains how a developer obtains a trusted fgOS runtime, how that runtime is selected for a workspace, and how doctor/repair keeps the environment usable.
Use this area when the work touches:
- install channels and release artifacts;
| Reader goal | Read |
| Understand the direction and why this area exists | [vision.md](vision.md) |
When sources disagree, read them in this order:
| Source class | Use for | Do not use for |
The area has two live runtime layers:
| Layer | Status | Meaning |
Packaging-distribution owns the question:
Which fgOS runtime is selected, trusted, activated, repaired, upgraded, and
allowed to mutate this workspace?
| Term | Meaning |
| `fgctl` | Machine/global bootstrap command. Installs, stages, verifies, activates, repairs, and upgrades fgOS runtimes. |
Packaging-distribution owns a platform-support component in the whole-system boundary map:
| Boundary question | Answer |
Any maintained doc in this area that states a design claim must identify its implementation status:
| Status | Meaning |
The old sources are preserved during migration:
- `docs/specs/distribution.md` remains the legacy/generated-curated spec source.
- `docs/distribution-vision.md` is promoted into `vision.md`; the old path remains historical source material until redirected.

| area vision | [vision.md](vision.md) |
